signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: The G10 scorecard records USD outperforming the board at +1.499% across 9 pairs while NOK lags at -1.994% across 2 pairs, generating a 3.493% leader-to-laggard spread that triggers the critical bilateral threshold. USD/NOK trades at 9.506, holding above its SMA20 at 9.354, SMA50 at 9.406, and SMA200 at 9.488. The carry backdrop reflects structural policy divergence, with Fed policy at 4.00% versus Norges Bank at 4.50%, while market expectations price further Fed tightening following hot US CPI releases. Retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data shows an extreme 91% long positioning, presenting contrarian positioning friction even as spot clears its prior 10-day closing high. The technical structure confirms spot trading entirely above its 20-day moving average following a wide-range expansion bar. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK, momentum supported by broad dollar strength across G10. Catalyst: Fed meeting 9 Dec — hike bias priced. Risk: Retracement and daily close below the SMA200 at 9.488 invalidating the breakout structure.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium + Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.68, holding firmly above its SMA20 at 157.95, SMA50 at 157.24, and SMA200 at 158.61. The OIS differential provides an authoritative carry baseline, with SOFR at 3.88% versus TONA at 1.23% yielding a +265bp advantage that favors the dollar. Meanwhile, 25-delta risk reversals print an extreme put skew of -1.87 (1M tenor, Saxo Bank), indicating heavy options demand for downside protection against potential official action. Intraday price action holds just below 160.00, the psychological mark that previously triggered Ministry of Finance warnings and intervention concerns. The divergence between resilient spot carry flows and elevated downside options hedging points to distribution near the highs rather than an unhedged trend advance. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY, elevated barrier tension beneath official intervention territory. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Dec — hike bias priced. Risk: Sustained daily close above 160.00 without official pushback, forcing options short-gamma unwinds.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + Retail Long Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1096, entrenched below its SMA20 at 1.1197, SMA50 at 1.1330, and SMA200 at 1.1542. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds net short EUR by -104,030 contracts, sitting at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.80, marking an institutional positioning extreme. In sharp contrast, Retail sentiment data retail sentiment registers 85% long, establishing an acute institutional-versus-retail divergence at the bottom of the range. Policy rate differentials reinforce the dollar's advantage, with the Fed at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65%, providing a 135bp spread in favor of the dollar that limits structural euro upside. With 1M ATM implied volatility at 5.8% running roughly in line with 30-day realized volatility at 6.0% (VRP -0.1%), the market is not paying up for downside acceleration. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, institutional short trend entrenched against trapped retail longs. Catalyst: Euro Area GDP on 12 Nov — 0.4% q/q forecast. Risk: Leverage fund short covering lifting price above the SMA20 at 1.1197.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Downtrend Extension + OIS Carry Deficit
signals.text: AUD/USD prints at 0.6853, positioned entirely below its SMA20 at 0.6984, SMA50 at 0.7037, and SMA200 at 0.7059, confirming an active downtrend. Leveraged fund positioning holds net long at +43,532 contracts, but sentiment is eroding as net exposure dropped WoW by -395 and 4W by -5,379. Despite the RBA cash rate at 4.85% maintaining a 97bp OIS carry premium over SOFR at 3.88% (AONIA 4.85% vs SOFR 3.88%), the currency remains weighed down by broad US dollar yield momentum following recent inflation prints. The technical trend structure highlights the pair trading extended at 2.43 ATR below its 20-day average following a clean break below 0.6905 support. With the Economic Surprise Index for AUD at -5.5, macro fundamentals are failing to validate the residual speculative long overhang. Trade bias: Short AUD/USD, trend continuation breaking key moving average bands. Catalyst: RBA meeting 8 Dec — hold stance expected. Risk: Rebound and close back above the 0.6905 breakdown level.
